coverage_notes:
Consolidated the 4-angle pool (54 raw rows) into 33 deduped sources for exercise/techniques. Tier mix favors high grade: 10 T0 (metas/systematic reviews), 14 T1 (RCTs, mostly trained/recreational subjects), 6 T2 (expert consensus), 3 T3 (practitioner/originator) — within the requested ~20-35 band and T0/T1/T2-weighted.

DEDUP DECISIONS (URL-level, plus same-article merges keeping canonical PMC/abstract over paywalled/blocked mirrors):
- Angleri 2017: kept Springer full text (reference-only) + PubMed abstract (28130627) — both retained because Springer is paywalled and PubMed is the accessible methods/results source for this load-bearing seed-chase RCT.
- Enes/Prestes 2021 (34260860): appeared 3x -> one row.
- Sodal 2023 drop-set meta: kept PMC10390395; dropped Springer mirror s40798-023-00620-5 (same CC-BY article).
- Havers 2026 drop-set meta: kept PMC13043944; dropped Springer mirror s40798-026-01012-1.
- Tsartsapakis 2026: appeared as PMC12922048 (two URL forms) + MDPI 11/1/80 (403'd WebFetch) -> one canonical PMC row.
- Zhang/Weakley 2025 superset meta: kept PMC12011898; dropped Springer mirror s40279-025-02176-8.
- Iversen 'No Time to Lift' 2021: appeared 4x (Springer paywalled x2, PubMed 34125411, PMC8449772 open) -> single open PMC8449772 row.
- Cluster volume/effort-matched RCT: kept PMC12174233; noted Springer s00421-025-05712-6 is the same article.

NAMED AUTHORITIES (PLAN lines 90-114) — representation:
- Schoenfeld: present across 6 rows (2014/2016 loading RCTs, Coleman & Sodal metas as co-author, Fink RCT, SCJ drop-set review, Iversen review). STRONG.
- Angleri/Ugrinowitsch/Libardi (crescent pyramid): present (Springer + PubMed). STRONG.
- Coleman (drop-set meta): present.
- Fink, Ozaki (drop-set RCTs): both present.
- Prestes / Enes (rest-pause): present (Prestes 2019 + Enes 2021).
- Cluster reviews: Davies + Jukic metas present. NOTE: PLAN names 'Tufano et al.' specifically; no clean Tufano canonical URL surfaced in the pool, but the Davies (chronic) + Jukic (acute) Sports Medicine metas plus the Lidsen short review fully cover cluster-set chronic/acute/scoping — Tufano's work is cited within these. Tufano not added as a standalone to avoid inventing a URL.
- Fagerli (myo-reps originator): ADDED borgefagerli.com (verified resolvable) + Barbell Medicine myo-reps explainer, since the pool had myo-reps RCTs but not the originator/effective-reps mechanistic source the PLAN names.
- Iversen / Weakley (supersets/time-efficiency): both present (Iversen review; Weakley as Zhang 2025 superset meta co-author + SportRxiv RCT).
- SBS/MASS (Nuckols/Helms/Zourdos): present (SBS pyramid + SBS drop-sets).
- RP/Israetel: present (intensity-techniques article).
- Brook Bush: present (drop-set systematic review).
- Pre-exhaust refutation: present x3 (Fujita untrained EMG, trained-men EMG, narrative review) — covers the PLAN's claim-7 refutation with the training-status gap closed.

AUTHORITIES NOTED-BUT-NOT-ADDED (no clean/redistributable canonical URL in the verified pool; would require inventing or citing a paywalled bookstore page):
- Helms/3DMJ as standalone: covered indirectly via MASS co-authorship (SBS rows) and the Muscle & Strength Pyramid book (search surfaced only Amazon/Goodreads/studylib copies — not a citable primary, so omitted). Note for Phase B if a clean 3DMJ article URL is wanted.
- Henselmans: no canonical article URL appeared in the pool or my verification searches; omitted rather than invented. Flag as a Phase-A gap if his bayesian-meta or rest-pause commentary is desired.
- Schoenfeld 'Science and Development of Muscle Hypertrophy' textbook (T2): no redistributable URL; the textbook's positions are covered by the Schoenfeld-authored journal rows.

CONFLATION-GUARD READINESS: every 'superior' claim in the PLAN's Phase-D seed list has >=1 volume-equated source attached — pyramid/crescent (Angleri equated TTV, Schoenfeld 2014/2016, Cardozo review), drop-set (Sodal/Havers/Coleman metas + Angleri/Fink/Ozaki equated RCTs), rest-pause (Enes equated; Prestes flagged NOT fully equated), myo-reps (RCT + thesis, ~equal at less volume), cluster (volume- AND effort-matched RCT + metas), pre-exhaust (EMG refutations + review). Practitioner/originator sources (SBS, RP, Fagerli, MuscleEvo, M&S) are tagged T2/T3 reference-only and flagged for PRACTICAL claims only, never to override an equated RCT.

PARSER: all 'trafilatura'; no github-md sources (no GitHub/markdown repos in scope). Flagged fetch hazards in notes: MDPI 403 (dropped in favor of PMC), SBS Cloudflare 403 (browser/trafilatura fallback), hal.science bot-block (De Camargo -> MDPI publisher page kept as canonical despite its own 403, since no open mirror resolved).

LICENSE: 16 redistribute-ok (PMC-OA/CC-BY/MDPI-OA/SportRxiv/institutional repo), 17 reference-only (paywalled journals: Springer/Thieme/JSCR/APNM/LWW/ScienceDirect; proprietary blogs: SBS/RP/Brookbush/M&S/MuscleEvo/Fagerli; ResearchGate copies of paywalled papers). No 'unknown' remain — the one pool 'unknown' (cluster EJAP 2025) was resolved to redistribute-ok via its CC-BY PMC mirror PMC12174233.

sources.title: Crescent pyramid and drop-set systems do not promote greater strength gains, muscle hypertrophy, and changes on muscle architecture compared with traditional resistance training in well-trained men (Angleri, Ugrinowitsch & Libardi, 2017, Eur J Appl Physiol)
sources.notes: SEED reference-chase target AND the canonical volume-equated crescent-pyramid + drop-set RCT in well-trained men. 12-wk within-subject, TTV-equalized; CSA increased similarly (TRAD 7.6%/CP 7.5%/DS 7.8%) and 1RM similarly. Spine of the 'pyramid/drop-set not superior' effect verdict. Springer full text paywalled; pair with the PubMed abstract (exercise-techniques-angleri-2017-pubmed) for accessible methods/results.

sources.title: Angleri et al. 2017 crescent pyramid / drop-set vs traditional RT in well-trained men — PubMed abstract record (PMID 28130627)
sources.notes: Free-text abstract + metadata for the Angleri 2017 RCT; use when the Springer full text is paywalled. Records design, equalized TTV, and the equivalent-hypertrophy/strength finding for the studies table.

sources.title: Effects of Varied Versus Constant Loading Zones on Muscular Adaptations in Trained Men (Schoenfeld et al., 2016, Int J Sports Med)
sources.notes: Schoenfeld RCT, 19 trained men, 8 wk: varied loading (2-4 / 8-12 / 20-30 RM, pyramid-style) vs constant 8-12 RM. Both increased strength, muscle thickness, endurance with no between-group difference. Supports pyramid/varied-load equivalence. PubMed abstract; Thieme full text paywalled.

sources.title: Effects of different volume-equated resistance training loading strategies on muscular adaptations in well-trained men (Schoenfeld et al., 2014, J Strength Cond Res)
sources.notes: Foundational volume-equated RCT in well-trained men comparing heavy/powerlifting-style vs moderate/bodybuilding-style loading; underpins the volume-equated loading-scheme literature behind pyramid-vs-straight comparisons. PubMed; JSCR full text paywalled.

sources.title: Pyramidal resistance training: A brief review of acute responses and long-term adaptations (Cardozo & Destro, 2023, J Bodywork Mov Ther)
sources.notes: Dedicated pyramid review: 15 studies (6 acute, 9 longitudinal), pyramidal vs traditional RT. Conclusion: pyramid not superior on acute physiology, strength, or hypertrophy. PubMed canonical; ScienceDirect full text paywalled.

sources.title: Pyramidal Systems in Resistance Training (De Camargo et al., 2021, Encyclopedia, MDPI)
sources.notes: Open-access (CC-BY) review/encyclopedia entry on pyramidal systems (ascending, descending/crescent, triangle) vs traditional RT; concludes half-triangle pyramid and traditional are equivalent for strength/hypertrophy. MDPI 403'd WebFetch and hal.science mirror is bot-blocked, so this is the canonical reference; trafilatura/browser fetch may be needed.

sources.title: Comparison of Traditional and Advanced Resistance Training Paradigms on Muscle Hypertrophy in Trained Individuals: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (Fonseca et al., 2023, Transl Sports Med)
sources.notes: Open-access (CC-BY) meta-analysis, 10 RCTs in trained individuals comparing advanced systems (pyramid, crescent pyramid, drop-set, pre-exhaustion, rest-pause) vs traditional. No superior hypertrophy for advanced systems. PMC full text confirmed open.

sources.title: Effects of Advanced Resistance Training Systems on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength in Recreationally Trained Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (Tsartsapakis et al., 2026, J Funct Morphol Kinesiol)
sources.notes: Open-access (CC-BY 4.0) meta-analysis, 23 studies, recreationally trained adults; pools drop sets, crescent pyramid (Angleri), rest-pause, cluster, tempo. Small strength benefit for advanced; no hypertrophy advantage when volume/effort matched; ~halved training time; modest rest-pause hypertrophy edge. Canonical PMC; MDPI publisher mirror (mdpi.com/2411-5142/11/1/80) 403'd WebFetch so dropped in favor of this.

sources.title: The Effects of Advanced Resistance Training Prescription Methods on Strength, Power, Hypertrophy, and Performance Adaptations in Healthy Adults: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-analysis (Sports Medicine, 2026)
sources.notes: Bayesian network meta-analysis ranking advanced RT methods (incl. pyramid/varied loading, drop-set, rest-pause, cluster) vs traditional and each other for strength, power, hypertrophy, jump, sprint. No clear evidence advanced methods beat traditional. Springer page paywalled; open PDF mirror reportedly at fisiologiadelejercicio.com.

sources.title: Maximizing Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review of Advanced Resistance Training Techniques and Methods (Krzysztofik, Wilk, Wojdala, Golas, 2019, IJERPH)
sources.notes: Broad systematic review of advanced techniques: supersets (agonist-antagonist + upper-lower), drop sets, pre-exhaustion, cluster sets, accentuated eccentric, BFR. PMC-OA (MDPI CC-BY). Supplies mechanism text and best_for/contraindication framing for many set_structures rows; notes pre-exhaust decreased reps on the multi-joint lift.

sources.title: Effects of Drop Sets on Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis (Sodal, Kristiansen, Larsen, van den Tillaar, 2023, Sports Medicine - Open)
sources.notes: ANCHOR for the drop-set effect claim. CC-BY 4.0, PMC-OA. 6 studies/142 subjects: no significant hypertrophy difference vs traditional, most volume-equated (flags Varovic as non-equated confound, sensitivity-stable); drop sets achieve equal growth in ~1/2 to 1/3 the time. Effect=equivalent / practical=time-efficiency. Springer mirror (s40798-023-00620-5) deduped in favor of this canonical PMC page.

sources.title: Muscular Adaptations in Drop Set vs. Traditional Training: A Meta-Analysis (Coleman, Grgic, Schoenfeld et al., 2022, Int J Strength & Conditioning)
sources.notes: Named-authority Coleman drop-set meta (5 studies): trivial ES favoring drop sets for hypertrophy (0.08) and strength (0.07) = equivalent. CC-BY, PDF available; verified resolvable. The meta reviewed by the SBS/MASS analysis below.

sources.title: Acute and Chronic Effects of Drop-Set Training: A Meta-Analysis and Systematic Review (Havers, Micke, Geisler, Held, 2026, Sports Medicine - Open)
sources.notes: Newest (2026) drop-set meta covering acute (RPE, lactate, HR) and chronic (hypertrophy/strength/endurance) effects. PMC-OA CC-BY. Conclusion: comparable long-term adaptations vs traditional; time-efficient (needs 1/2-1/3 the time) but higher perceptual/neuromuscular demand needing recovery management. Updates Sodal 2023. Springer mirror (s40798-026-01012-1) deduped in favor of this PMC page.

sources.title: Effects of drop set resistance training on acute stress indicators and long-term muscle hypertrophy and strength (Fink, Schoenfeld et al., 2018, J Sports Med Phys Fitness)
sources.notes: Named-authority Fink 6-week RCT (triceps pressdown): drop-set vs conventional, volume-matched. Similar strength gains, drop-set group significantly shorter sessions = foundational time-efficiency RCT. ResearchGate copy of paywalled journal.

sources.title: Effects of drop sets with resistance training on increases in muscle CSA, strength, and endurance: a pilot study (Ozaki et al., 2018, J Sports Sci)
sources.notes: Named-authority Ozaki RCT: high-load 3 sets vs low-load 3 sets vs single high-load set + descending drop sets. Similar muscle growth; 1RM strength favored high-load-inclusive protocols. PubMed record; J Sports Sci paywalled.

sources.title: Drop Sets: Comprehensive Systematic Review and Training Recommendations (Brookbush Institute)
sources.notes: Named-authority (Brook Bush) systematic review of drop sets with practitioner training recommendations; synthesizes the RCT literature for application. Proprietary site, reference-only.

sources.title: Can You Drop (Set) Weight for Gains? (Stronger By Science / MASS, reviewing Coleman et al. meta-analysis)
sources.notes: Named-authority SBS/MASS (Nuckols/Helms/Zourdos) analysis of the Coleman drop-set meta; practical verdict: drop sets as a secondary volume tool, not standalone for big lifts. Expert practitioner synthesis. Proprietary blog; supports practical claims only.

sources.title: Can Drop Set Training Enhance Muscle Growth? (Schoenfeld & Grgic, 2018, Strength & Conditioning Journal)
sources.notes: Named-authority NSCA SCJ narrative review by Schoenfeld & Grgic on drop-set mechanisms (failure, metabolic stress) and evidence. Expert/textbook-grade; LWW journal paywalled.

sources.title: Rest-pause and drop-set training elicit similar strength and hypertrophy adaptations compared with traditional sets in resistance-trained males (Enes, Prestes et al., 2021, Appl Physiol Nutr Metab)
sources.notes: ANCHOR RCT for rest-pause AND drop-set in TRAINED males (28 men, back squat), 8-wk volume-equated. No superior hypertrophy from advanced techniques; rest-pause slightly favored for strength. Drives the rest-pause 'disputed growth edge / time-efficiency' verdict. PubMed abstract; APNM full text paywalled. (Appeared 3x in pool, deduped to one.)

sources.title: Strength and Muscular Adaptations Following 6 Weeks of Rest-Pause vs. Traditional Multiple-Sets Resistance Training in Trained Subjects (Prestes et al., 2019, J Strength Cond Res)
sources.notes: Named-authority Prestes rest-pause RCT, frequently cited as favoring rest-pause for thigh hypertrophy and local muscular endurance vs traditional sets in trained men (note: not fully volume-equated — flag as a conflation-guard candidate). ResearchGate PDF; JSCR paywalled.

sources.title: Effect of rest-pause vs. traditional bench press training on muscle strength, electromyography, and lifting volume (Korak et al., 2017)
sources.notes: RCT comparing rest-pause vs traditional bench press: similar 1RM gains, with EMG and lifting-volume differences. Supports rest-pause strength equivalence. PubMed abstract.

sources.title: Twelve Weeks Rest-Pause and Traditional Resistance Training: Effects on Myokines and Performance Adaptations among Recreationally Trained Men
sources.notes: 12-wk rest-pause vs traditional RCT covering performance and myokine (mechanistic) responses. MDPI open access (CC-BY). Provides mechanistic + chronic data for the rest-pause row.

sources.title: Similar Strength and Hypertrophic Adaptations in Less Time? Myo-Reps vs. Traditional Straight-Sets in Resistance-Trained Men
sources.notes: ANCHOR myo-reps RCT in TRAINED men: similar muscle size/strength/excitation vs traditional straight sets despite ~30% less volume load and less time. Converts the myo-reps verdict from 'disputed/mechanistic-only' toward 'equivalent with a time-efficiency win.' PubMed abstract; full text paywalled.

sources.title: Comparing Physiological, Psychological, and Performance Changes Between Myo-Reps Vs Traditional Hypertrophy Protocols (Liberty University doctoral thesis)
sources.notes: Open-access thesis: 8-wk myo-reps vs traditional, gains in both groups, no between-group differences in size/strength/excitation/velocity, myo-reps ~30% less volume load. Free full text (institutional repository) backing myo-reps effective-reps practical claim and effect equivalence.

sources.title: Borge Fagerli — Coach & Creator of Myo-Reps (originator site)
sources.notes: Named PLAN authority (Fagerli, myo-reps originator). Primary source for the myo-reps protocol definition and the 'effective/stimulating reps' model (final ~5 reps near failure drive growth). Use for concepts/mechanism text only; effect grade is T3 mechanistic, never to override an RCT. Verified resolvable.

sources.title: Myo-Reps (Barbell Medicine)
sources.notes: Evidence-based practitioner explainer (Barbell Medicine) defining myo-reps and critically situating the effective-reps model against the RCT literature. Useful for concept definition + the 'mechanistic, not proven-superior' framing. Verified resolvable.

sources.title: Superset Versus Traditional Resistance Training Prescriptions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Exploring Acute and Chronic Effects on Mechanical, Metabolic, and Perceptual Variables (Zhang, Weakley, Li, Li, Garcia-Ramos, 2025, Sports Medicine)
sources.notes: ANCHOR for the superset effect claim (named authority Weakley). CC-BY 4.0, PMC-OA. No significant difference vs traditional for maximal strength (SMD 0.10), strength endurance (0.07), or hypertrophy (-0.05); supersets maintain equal volume in ~37% less session time but raise RPE/metabolic stress. Splits cleanly into effect=equivalent / practical=time-efficiency. Springer mirror (s40279-025-02176-8) deduped to this PMC page.

sources.title: Less time, same gains: Comparison of superset vs traditional set training on muscular adaptations (SportRxiv preprint, 2025)
sources.notes: Chronic RCT (trained participants) underpinning the superset meta: superset training completed sessions in ~36% less time with similar between-group hypertrophy/strength changes. Open preprint (SportRxiv, openly licensed); published version on ScienceDirect (paywalled).

sources.title: Agonist-Antagonist Paired Set Resistance Training: A Brief Review (Robbins, Young, Behm)
sources.notes: Foundational review of antagonist/AAPS supersets: mechanisms (reciprocal innervation, reduced antagonist braking) and the conclusion that the real benefit is training DENSITY / time-efficiency, with limited acute performance boost and greater fatigue. Mechanism + practical-claim source for the antagonist-superset row. ResearchGate copy.

sources.title: The Pre-Exhaustion Method Does Not Increase Muscle Activity in Target Muscle During Strength Training in Untrained Individuals (Fujita, Silva, Bedo, Gomes, 2022, J Human Kinetics)
sources.notes: REFUTATION source for the pre-exhaust 'shifts the stimulus' folklore. CC BY-NC-ND, PMC-OA. EMG study: pre-exhaustion did NOT increase target (lat) activation. Conflation-guard caveat: subjects UNTRAINED and outcome is EMG (not growth) — supports a refuted/practical claim only.

sources.title: Comparison Between Pre-Exhaustion and Traditional Exercise Order on Muscle Activation and Performance in Trained Men
sources.notes: Pre-exhaust refutation in TRAINED men (closes the training-status gap left by the untrained EMG paper). Pre-exhaustion order did not preferentially shift activation onto the target muscle and reduced performance/volume on the subsequent multi-joint lift. PMC-OA; confirm exact license on fetch.

sources.title: Pre-exhaustion Training, a Narrative Review of the Acute Responses and Chronic Adaptations
sources.notes: Narrative review consolidating the pre-exhaust evidence base — acute EMG/performance reductions plus thin chronic-adaptation data. PMC-OA. Supplies mechanism + verdict framing for the pre-exhaust set_structures row and the refuted-folklore claim.

sources.title: Chronic Effects of Altering Resistance Training Set Configurations Using Cluster Sets: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (Davies et al., 2021, Sports Medicine)
sources.notes: Cornerstone meta-analysis on chronic strength/power/hypertrophy adaptations of cluster set configurations and intra-set rest. Supports the 'cluster = power/velocity-maintenance, no clear hypertrophy edge' verdict. Springer paywalled.

sources.title: Acute Effects of Cluster and Rest Redistribution Set Structures on Mechanical, Metabolic, and Perceptual Fatigue During and After Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis (Jukic et al., 2020, Sports Medicine)
sources.notes: Quantifies the fatigue cost: cluster/rest-redistribution attenuate velocity/power/force loss and lower metabolic/perceptual fatigue vs traditional sets (effect sizes). Backbone for the cluster fatigue_cost field. Springer paywalled.

sources.title: Cluster sets and traditional sets elicit similar muscular hypertrophy: a volume- and effort-matched study in resistance-trained individuals (Eur J Appl Physiol 2025)
sources.notes: Volume- AND effort-matched within-participant unilateral cluster-set RCT in trained individuals: equated volume/RIR -> similar muscle thickness & lean mass for cluster vs traditional. Direct evidence preventing a cluster hypertrophy overclaim. CC-BY 4.0, PMC-OA. (Springer DOI s00421-025-05712-6 is the same article.)

sources.title: Cluster sets lead to better performance maintenance and minimize training-induced fatigue than traditional sets
sources.notes: Direct fatigue-cost evidence: cluster sets maintain velocity/power and reduce training-induced fatigue vs traditional sets. CC-BY, PMC-OA (Frontiers). Supports the cluster 'power/velocity-maintenance' real-use framing.

sources.title: Cluster Sets for Muscle Hypertrophy: A Short Review (OBM Integrative and Complementary Medicine)
sources.notes: Open-access short review framing cluster sets primarily as a velocity/power-maintenance and volume-redistribution tool rather than a hypertrophy method. Supplies mechanism + 'real use is power/velocity maintenance' scoping for the cluster set_structures row and the cluster claim's nuance.

sources.title: No Time to Lift? Designing Time-Efficient Training Programs for Strength and Hypertrophy: A Narrative Review (Iversen, Norum, Schoenfeld, Fimland, 2021, Sports Medicine)
sources.notes: UMBRELLA time-efficiency consensus review (named authorities Iversen + Schoenfeld). CC-BY 4.0, PMC-OA. Covers supersets, drop sets, rest-pause, cluster: roughly halve training time while maintaining volume. Backbone for cross-cutting time-efficiency practical claims; cite for practical, never to override an RCT. Deduped from 4 pooled URLs (Springer s40279-021-01490-1 paywalled + PubMed 34125411) to this open PMC page.

sources.title: Does pyramid training actually work? (Stronger By Science / Greg Nuckols & team)
sources.notes: Named-authority SBS/Nuckols evidence-based explainer synthesizing pyramid vs reverse-pyramid vs straight sets against the RCT/meta literature. Verdict: pyramid viable but on par with traditional when volume matched. Verified resolvable; WebFetch may hit Cloudflare 403 so prefer trafilatura/browser fetch. Practical claims only.

sources.title: How to Use Reverse Pyramid Training to Maximize Gains (Muscle & Strength)
sources.notes: Practitioner explainer with the operational definition/protocol of reverse pyramid training (RPT): heaviest set first after warm-up, ~8-10% load drops with rising reps. Supplies the RPT protocol/concept text to contrast against straight sets. Proprietary, reference-only.

sources.title: Pyramid Sets vs Reverse Pyramid Training vs Drop Sets (MuscleEvo / Christian Finn)
sources.notes: High-quality practitioner explainer contrasting straight pyramid, reverse pyramid (RPT), and drop sets, referencing the research consensus that volume/load/proximity-to-failure drive results. Useful for terminology/definitions of each scheme. Proprietary, reference-only.

sources.title: Intensity Techniques for Maximum Mass (RP Strength / Israetel)
sources.notes: Named PLAN authority (RP/Israetel) on when to deploy drop sets / rest-pause / myo-reps — limited doses, isolation/high-SFR exercises, final sets, not failure-prone grip-loaded compounds. Backs the cross-cutting practical claim ('intensity techniques quarantined to isolation') and the constraints hooks (left-pinky jam / failure-on-compounds). Proprietary blog, reference-only.
